candidate.title: DLAF
candidate.scope: The DLAF (Directly Ligate Sequencing Adapters to the First-Strand cDNA) middle-row schematic: random-primed mRNA conversion to first-strand cDNA, RNA removal, direct splinted attachment of left/right adapters, USER removal of adapter splints, and PCR/purification. This is one linear target workflow. The neighboring TRAP-Seq, miTRAP and partially visible upper row, and the chemical drawings at the far right, are surrounding poster context. Paper comparisons with dUTP or ScriptSeq are not depicted DLAF alternatives. The endpoint is a sequencing library, with sequencing itself unshown.

features: Terminal depicted material is labeled cDNA after PCR and purify; the final simple line is a schematic library endpoint.
Sequenced material is DNA derived from first-strand cDNA; it represents sampled mRNA sequences with strand orientation retained through distinct adapters.
The paper reports that read_1 is in the transcription direction and read_2 is sequenced from the other end; no sequencing or analysis operation is drawn in this row.
Direct ligation preserves RNA-end information present in the first-strand cDNA; this is transcriptome coverage, not evidence that every insert spans an intact transcript.

evidence.quote: Read_1 indicates the reads in the direction of transcription. Read_2 indicates the reads sequenced from the other end of the cDNA molecules.

evidence.rationale: The paper frames full-length as coverage across transcript ends and the schematic uses random priming; neither establishes that each library insert is an intact full-length transcript.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: The depicted random primer supports copying mRNA into first-strand cDNA. RNA remains in the product before the next RNase step.
operations.mechanism: Primer-directed reverse transcription produces DNA complementary to RNA; 5′-phosphorylated random primers supply the cDNA phosphate used at the later ligation interface.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is transferred to a complementary first-strand DNA carrier. This local route depicts random priming, without an explicit end-specific selection.

evidence.quote: RT was carried out with random oligomers with a phosphate group at their 5′ end to obviate the phosphorylation step.

operations.label: RNase digestion
operations.description: Digestion removes the RNA associated with the reverse-transcription product, leaving single-stranded first-strand cDNA for direct adapter attachment.
operations.mechanism: Ribonuclease digestion of RNA; the paper confirms single-stranded DNA as the retained product.
operations.information_effect: The RNA template is discarded while its complementary DNA sequence is retained.

operations.label: Ligation in presence of PEG and DMSO
operations.description: Both double-stranded adapters are joined to the ends of the same first-strand cDNA insert. The random-overhang splints anneal to insert ends; each opposing adapter strand is covalently ligated. PEG and DMSO are depicted additives, not separate input branches.
operations.mechanism: Splint-assisted DNA ligation: the LEFT ligating strand joins its 5′ phosphate to the cDNA 3′ end, and the RIGHT ligating strand joins its 3′ end to the cDNA 5′ phosphate. The marked 3′ hexanediol groups limit unwanted concatenation.
operations.information_effect: Different adapter sequences mark the two ends of the original first-strand carrier, preserving the association between insert sequence and RNA strand. The overhang Ns are annealing aids on removable strands, not depicted molecular identifiers.

operations.label: Uracil-specific excision (USER)
operations.description: USER removes the uracil-containing non-ligating adapter strands. The insert and the covalently joined blue/red adapter strands remain as one adapter-flanked single strand.
operations.mechanism: Selective degradation of deoxyuridine-containing adapter splints, rather than degradation of a second-strand cDNA insert.
operations.information_effect: Removes temporary annealing strands while retaining insert sequence and adapter polarity.

operations.label: PCR and purify
operations.description: The adapter-flanked first-strand product is PCR-amplified and purified, yielding the terminal cDNA library. These two actions remain one block at the resolution shown.
operations.mechanism: PCR amplifies adapter-bearing DNA; purification yields the represented library product.
operations.information_effect: The amplified DNA library reports sampled transcript sequence and strand. Direct adapter attachment avoids a separate second-strand cDNA preparation before ligation; it does not mean that PCR makes no complementary DNA.

method_scopes.rationale: The card names DLAF and the image expands that name beside the middle workflow. The catalogue heading and its schematic caption independently identify the same target. Agarwal et al. describe the same direct ligation of adapters to RNase-generated first-strand cDNA and removal of uracil-bearing adapter strands. All five operation instances apply to this schematic; no neighboring method or paper comparison is added. The diagram shows NNNNN overhangs as a representative adapter; the paper specifies five- and six-base forms. Its oligo sequences also resolve which 3′ termini are blocked and which must remain ligatable. The paper also used an anchored oligo(dT) primer in addition to random primers; that unshown primer component and its dedicated poly(A)-site interpretation are not assigned to the depicted random-primer operation. The random-overhang splints are temporary ligation components; they are not retained molecular barcodes. The secondary page also cites a Nussbacher review and an Iwase application paper. Those are catalogue-only background here; neither primary publication was inspected or used as reaction evidence, and neither broadens the DLAF target.
